entities.name: Lung adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Think receptor–RAS–RAF drivers; keep mutations, amplifications and fusions separate.
snv: Driver — EGFR activating SNVs/indels; KRAS; BRAF (including V600E); ERBB2 activating variants (distinct subsets)
Driver — MET splice-site variants causing exon 14 skipping; less often NF1 loss or RIT1 activation
Cooperating — TP53, STK11, KEAP1, SMARCA4 inactivation
cnv: Driver — focal high-level MET or ERBB2 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — CDKN2A deletion; MYC amplification
rearr: Driver — EML4::ALK; CD74::ROS1; KIF5B::RET / CCDC6::RET (examples; alternative partners)
Driver — NTRK1/2/3 or NRG1 fusions (rare; NRG1 enriched in mucinous tumors)
entities.pitfall: A list represents alternative molecular subsets, not mutations expected together in every tumor. MET exon 14 skipping is a splicing consequence, not a gene fusion.

entities.name: Lung squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Squamous lung: TP53 plus cell-cycle/PI3K alterations.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, CDKN2A loss; PIK3CA activation; PTEN loss
Cooperating — NFE2L2 activation; KEAP1 and NOTCH1 loss
cnv: Characteristic — SOX2/TP63 (3q) amplification; FGFR1 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — CDKN2A deletion
other: Viral — EBV in many pulmonary lymphoepithelial carcinomas, a squamous subtype
entities.pitfall: A squamous phenotype does not imply EGFR or ALK-driven disease; SOX2/TP63 gain is a lineage-associated event.

entities.name: Lung adenosquamous carcinoma
entities.anchor: Two morphologies can share one lung adenocarcinoma-type driver.
snv: Driver — EGFR or KRAS activating variants in subsets
Cooperating — TP53 alterations
rearr: Driver — ALK and other kinase fusions can occur (uncommon)
entities.pitfall: Molecular findings overlap adenocarcinoma; both components do not require separate drivers.

entities.name: Lung large cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: An exclusion diagnosis with no defining molecular switch.
snv: Driver/cooperating — heterogeneous NSCLC-type changes, including TP53; KRAS in a subset
entities.pitfall: Requires exclusion of glandular, squamous and neuroendocrine differentiation; no single defining recurrent driver established.

entities.name: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma
entities.anchor: MET exon 14 skipping is a memorable enrichment.
snv: Driver — MET splice alterations causing exon 14 skipping; KRAS activating variants (subsets)
Cooperating — TP53 loss
cnv: Cooperating — MDM2 amplification in a subset
entities.pitfall: Includes pleomorphic, spindle/giant-cell carcinoma and carcinosarcoma for study; MET alteration is not universal.

entities.name: Pulmonary blastoma
entities.anchor: Adult biphasic blastoma: DICER1 plus Wnt.
snv: Driver — DICER1 pathogenic variants
Driver — CTNNB1 exon 3 hotspot variants (often co-occurring)
entities.pitfall: Different entity from childhood pleuropulmonary blastoma, despite shared DICER1 biology.

entities.name: Small cell lung carcinoma
entities.anchor: Small cell: lose TP53 and RB1.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and RB1 biallelic inactivation
Cooperating — NOTCH-family loss-of-function variants
cnv: Driver/cooperating — RB1/TP53 deletions; MYC, MYCL or MYCN amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: TP53/RB1 loss is characteristic but not absolutely universal; combined histology is included.

entities.name: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of lung
entities.anchor: LCNEC can follow either TP53/RB1 or TP53/STK11–KEAP1 patterns.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 with RB1 loss in one major subset
Driver/cooperating — STK11, KEAP1, KRAS alterations in another subset
cnv: Cooperating — RB1 deletion; MYC-family amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: LCNEC and carcinoid are different biological classes; not all LCNEC has RB1 loss.

entities.name: Pulmonary carcinoid tumor
entities.anchor: Carcinoid favors MEN1/chromatin biology over the classic small-cell pair.
snv: Driver — MEN1 inactivation (subset)
Cooperating — chromatin-regulator alterations including ARID1A and EIF1AX (subsets)
cnv: Characteristic — 11q/MEN1 loss and other variable arm-level losses
entities.pitfall: Typical and atypical carcinoids are merged; both have malignant potential. TP53/RB1 alterations are not their usual baseline signature.

entities.name: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor
entities.anchor: Undifferentiated thoracic tumor: lose SMARCA4/BRG1.
snv: Driver — SMARCA4 inactivating variants
Cooperating — TP53, KRAS, STK11 or KEAP1 alterations (subsets)
cnv: Driver — SMARCA4 deletion / second-allele loss
other: Phenotype — SMARCA2 protein loss is frequent, often without a corresponding gene mutation
entities.pitfall: SMARCA4-deficient conventional NSCLC is not automatically this entity; morphology and immunophenotype matter.

entities.name: Pulmonary mucoepidermoid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Mucoepidermoid: MAML2 fusion.
rearr: Driver — CRTC1::MAML2; less often CRTC3::MAML2
entities.pitfall: Fusion-negative tumors exist; distinguish from ordinary adenosquamous carcinoma.

entities.name: Pulmonary adenoid cystic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Adenoid cystic: MYB-family transcriptional activation.
rearr: Driver — MYB::NFIB or other MYB rearrangements (subset)
entities.pitfall: A negative MYB break-apart test does not exclude adenoid cystic carcinoma.

entities.name: Pulmonary epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
entities.anchor: A rare biphasic salivary-type lung tumor without a firmly established recurrent driver.
entities.pitfall: Do not assume that the HRAS frequencies of salivary-gland counterparts apply to lung cases; molecular evidence remains limited.

entities.name: Pulmonary hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Clear cells in hyaline stroma: EWSR1::ATF1.
rearr: Driver — EWSR1::ATF1 (characteristic)
entities.pitfall: EWSR1 rearrangement alone is nonspecific; gene partner, morphology and site determine the diagnosis.

entities.name: Thymoma
entities.anchor: Thymoma: remember GTF2I, especially A/AB morphology.
snv: Driver — GTF2I p.L424H hotspot (enriched in type A/AB)
Driver — HRAS/NRAS alterations (minor subset)
cnv: Characteristic — variable aneuploidy; CDKN2A/B deletion in some advanced tumors
entities.pitfall: A, AB and B1–B3 are merged. Thymoma can invade or metastasize even when cytologically bland.

entities.name: Thymic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Thymic carcinoma: TP53/CDKN2A; KIT mutation is a minority.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and CDKN2A inactivation
Driver — KIT activating variants (subset); PI3K-pathway alterations (subset)
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion
entities.pitfall: CD117/KIT protein expression is much more common than activating KIT mutation. Histologic subtypes are merged.

entities.name: Thymic neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Thymic carcinoid can connect to MEN1.
snv: Driver — MEN1 loss (subset, sporadic or hereditary)
Cooperating — chromatin/mTOR-pathway alterations are heterogeneous
cnv: Characteristic — variable chromosomal losses and gains
entities.pitfall: Typical/atypical carcinoids are merged; do not transfer the lung small-cell signature to all thymic NETs.

entities.name: Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma
entities.anchor: High-grade thymic NEC often disrupts cell-cycle tumor suppressors.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and RB1 inactivation in subsets
cnv: Characteristic — marked copy-number instability in many high-grade tumors
entities.pitfall: Small- and large-cell NEC are merged; thymic data are smaller than pulmonary cohorts.

entities.name: Mesothelioma
entities.anchor: Mesothelioma: BAP1, NF2 and CDKN2A tumor-suppressor losses.
snv: Driver — BAP1 and NF2 inactivation
Cooperating — SETD2, TP53 and Hippo-pathway alterations (subsets)
cnv: Driver/cooperating — CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, often with MTAP co-deletion; BAP1/NF2 loss
entities.pitfall: Includes diffuse/localized invasive pleural and extrapleural forms. Peritoneal tumors have different alteration frequencies; no alteration alone establishes invasion.

entities.name: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Esophageal squamous: TP53 plus CCND1/SOX2.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, NOTCH1, CDKN2A inactivation; NFE2L2 activation
cnv: Driver/characteristic — CCND1, SOX2/TP63 and EGFR amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: HPV is not an established universal etiologic driver of esophageal squamous carcinoma.

entities.name: Esophageal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Esophageal adenocarcinoma often has unstable chromosomes and amplified receptors.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, CDKN2A, SMAD4 and ARID1A alterations
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
Characteristic — EGFR, KRAS, GATA4/GATA6 or CCNE1 amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Barrett-associated adenocarcinoma is molecularly distinct from squamous carcinoma.

entities.name: Gastric adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Stomach: receptors, adhesion/Wnt-like signaling, MSI or EBV pathways.
snv: Driver — CDH1 loss; RHOA or PIK3CA activation (different subsets)
Cooperating — TP53, ARID1A, APC or RNF43 alterations
cnv: Driver — ERBB2, FGFR2, MET or EGFR amplification (subsets)
Cooperating — CCNE1 amplification; CDKN2A deletion
rearr: Driver — CLDN18::ARHGAP26 / CLDN18::ARHGAP6 (subset)
other: Epigenetic — MLH1 promoter methylation can cause mismatch-repair deficiency/MSI
entities.pitfall: Intestinal, diffuse/poorly cohesive and other histologic variants are merged. CLDN18 protein expression is not the same finding as a CLDN18 gene fusion.

entities.name: Small intestinal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Small-bowel adenocarcinoma overlaps colon, with relatively more ERBB2 mutations.
snv: Driver/cooperating — KRAS, APC, TP53, SMAD4, PIK3CA alterations
Driver — ERBB2 activating variants; BRAF variants (often non-V600E)
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
other: Other — mismatch-repair deficiency/MSI in a subset
entities.pitfall: Do not assume all BRAF mutations are V600E or that small-bowel tumors have the same APC frequency as colon tumors.

entities.name: Ampullary adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Ampulla links intestinal APC and pancreatobiliary KRAS; remember ELF3.
snv: Driver/cooperating — APC, KRAS, TP53, SMAD4 and ELF3 inactivation/activation as appropriate
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
entities.pitfall: Intestinal and pancreatobiliary histologic subtypes are merged; they have different mutation distributions.

entities.name: Colorectal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Colon: APC → RAS/MAPK → TP53, with alternative MSI routes.
snv: Driver — APC loss; KRAS/NRAS or BRAF activation (alternative subsets)
Cooperating — TP53, SMAD4, PIK3CA and FBXW7 alterations
Driver — mismatch-repair gene inactivation or POLE proofreading variants (hypermutated subsets)
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — SMAD4/18q and CDKN2A losses
other: Epigenetic — MLH1 promoter methylation is a common sporadic cause of MSI
entities.pitfall: The sequence is a teaching model, not a required order. Mucinous, medullary and signet-ring patterns are included.

entities.name: Appendiceal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Appendix: KRAS/GNAS in mucinous tumors; TP53 with higher-grade disease.
snv: Driver — KRAS and GNAS activating variants (especially mucinous tumors)
Cooperating — TP53, SMAD4 or APC alterations in subsets
entities.pitfall: Invasive mucinous and conventional adenocarcinomas are included. Low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm is not automatically invasive adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Appendiceal goblet cell adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Goblet cell is adenocarcinoma; no single canonical fusion.
snv: Recurrent/candidate — TP53, ARID1A, RHOA, KDM6A and SOX9 alterations in subsets
entities.pitfall: Formerly called goblet cell carcinoid; it is not a conventional NET. KRAS/GNAS are less characteristic than in mucinous appendiceal tumors.

entities.name: Anal squamous cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Anal squamous: HPV E6/E7, with PI3K-pathway mutations.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA activation (subset)
Cooperating — TP53 and CDKN2A mutations enriched in HPV-negative disease
cnv: Cooperating — PIK3CA amplification or PTEN deletion (subsets)
other: Viral driver — high-risk HPV E6/E7 disrupt p53 and RB pathways
entities.pitfall: Viral inhibition of a tumor suppressor is not the same as an SNV in its gene.

entities.name: Anal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Anal gland/colorectal-type adenocarcinoma has heterogeneous genetics.
snv: Driver/cooperating — KRAS, TP53 and APC alterations can occur, depending on origin
entities.pitfall: Separate true anal primary from distal rectal extension; no single site-defining recurrent driver is established.

entities.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
entities.anchor: HCC: TERT promoter, TP53 and CTNNB1.
snv: Driver — TERT promoter activation; CTNNB1 activation; AXIN1 loss
Cooperating — TP53, ARID1A and ARID2 inactivation
cnv: Driver/cooperating — FGF19/CCND1 (11q13), MYC or MET amplification (subsets)
other: Other — HBV integration can activate TERT; HBV/HCV-associated chronic liver injury contributes to oncogenesis
entities.pitfall: TERT promoter changes are DNA variants outside coding exons. Etiology changes frequencies; no one alteration defines ordinary HCC.

entities.name: Fibrolamellar carcinoma
entities.anchor: Fibrolamellar: DNAJB1::PRKACA.
rearr: Driver — DNAJB1::PRKACA, usually from a focal chromosome 19 deletion
entities.pitfall: The fusion is highly characteristic in the right liver morphology but is not absolutely site-specific; interpret with pathology.

entities.name: Hepatoblastoma
entities.anchor: Hepatoblastoma: CTNNB1/Wnt in a young liver.
snv: Driver — CTNNB1 exon 3 SNVs/indels; APC loss in a minority
Cooperating — NFE2L2 activation (subset)
other: Predisposition — APC/FAP or 11p15 imprinting disorders in selected patients
entities.pitfall: Fetal, embryonal and mixed patterns are merged; most have fewer sequence alterations than adult HCC.

entities.name: Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Mixed liver lineage often shares TERT/TP53 alterations.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TERT promoter and TP53 variants; CTNNB1, KRAS, PTEN or chromatin-gene alterations in subsets
cnv: Cooperating — CCND1, MET or ERBB2 amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Genomic profiles can resemble HCC or CCA; diagnosis requires morphologic evidence of both differentiations.

entities.name: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Intrahepatic bile duct: FGFR2 fusions or IDH1/2 mutations in subsets.
snv: Driver — IDH1 R132 / IDH2 R172 variants; KRAS or BRAF activation (distinct subsets)
Cooperating — BAP1, ARID1A, PBRM1, TP53 alterations
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion
rearr: Driver — FGFR2::BICC1 and other FGFR2 fusions (many partners)
entities.pitfall: Small- versus large-duct patterns differ molecularly; FGFR2/IDH are enriched in small-duct tumors and are not universal.

entities.name: Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Extrahepatic bile duct: KRAS/TP53; occasional HER2.
snv: Driver/cooperating — KRAS, TP53, SMAD4, ARID1A alterations
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — CDKN2A deletion
rearr: Driver — ATP1B1::PRKACA / ATP1B1::PRKACB (rare)
entities.pitfall: Perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinomas are merged. Do not transfer intrahepatic FGFR2 fusion frequencies to extrahepatic disease.

entities.name: Gallbladder carcinoma
entities.anchor: Gallbladder: TP53 plus ERBB2 or KRAS in subsets.
snv: Driver — ERBB2, KRAS or PIK3CA activation (subsets)
Cooperating — TP53, CDKN2A and SMAD4 inactivation
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification
Cooperating — CDKN2A deletion
entities.pitfall: Adenocarcinoma and rare squamous/adenosquamous patterns are merged here; NEC is in the digestive NEC record.

entities.name: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Pancreatic ductal: KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A and SMAD4.
snv: Driver — KRAS activating variants
Cooperating — TP53, CDKN2A and SMAD4 inactivation
Driver/cooperating — BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2 defects in a minority; GNAS/RNF43 in some precursor-associated tumors
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A and SMAD4 deletions
entities.pitfall: Variants including adenosquamous, colloid and undifferentiated carcinomas are merged. KRAS-wild-type disease can harbor alternative kinase drivers.

entities.name: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Acinar: RAF fusion or DNA-repair loss, unlike the usual ductal KRAS pattern.
snv: Driver/cooperating — BRCA2/BRCA1 and other homologous-recombination repair defects; APC/CTNNB1 alterations (subsets)
cnv: Cooperating — variable tumor-suppressor losses
rearr: Driver — SND1::BRAF and other BRAF/RAF1 fusions (subset)
entities.pitfall: Pure and mixed acinar carcinomas are represented; usual PDAC driver combinations are less characteristic.

entities.name: Pancreatoblastoma
entities.anchor: Pancreatoblastoma: Wnt plus 11p.
snv: Driver — CTNNB1 activation or APC inactivation
cnv: Characteristic — 11p allelic loss (may be deletion or copy-neutral LOH)
other: Predisposition — APC/FAP or Beckwith–Wiedemann spectrum in some patients
entities.pitfall: Not the pediatric equivalent of ordinary KRAS-driven ductal adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of pancreas
entities.anchor: Solid pseudopapillary: CTNNB1 almost always leads.
snv: Driver — CTNNB1 exon 3 activating variants
entities.pitfall: This low-grade malignant neoplasm may behave indolently; CTNNB1 is shared with other tumors and requires the correct morphology.

entities.name: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: PanNET: MEN1, DAXX/ATRX and mTOR.
snv: Driver — MEN1, DAXX or ATRX inactivation
Driver — TSC1/TSC2, PTEN or other mTOR-pathway changes (subset)
cnv: Characteristic — recurrent chromosome losses, including MEN1/11q; heterogeneous gains
other: Other — alternative lengthening of telomeres associated with DAXX/ATRX loss
Predisposition — MEN1, VHL, NF1 or TSC syndromes in selected cases
entities.pitfall: G1–G3 and functional labels are merged. Well-differentiated G3 NET remains distinct from pancreatic NEC.

entities.name: Gastric neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Gastric NET often follows gastrin stimulation rather than a universal mutation.
snv: Predisposition/driver — MEN1 loss in MEN1-associated cases
other: Other — hypergastrinemia from autoimmune atrophic gastritis or gastrinoma can drive ECL-cell proliferation
entities.pitfall: Gastric NET categories and grades are merged; many sporadic tumors have no established recurrent defining genomic driver.

entities.name: Duodenal and ampullary neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Duodenal NET: consider MEN1 or NF1 context.
snv: Driver — NF1 biallelic inactivation in NF1-associated tumors
Predisposition/driver — MEN1 inactivation in a hereditary subset
entities.pitfall: Syndrome-associated changes do not apply to every sporadic tumor; hormonal variants are merged.

entities.name: Jejunoileal neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Midgut NET: chromosome 18 loss, occasional CDKN1B.
snv: Driver — CDKN1B inactivating variants (minor subset)
cnv: Characteristic — chromosome 18 loss; CDKN1B deletion (subset)
entities.pitfall: Most do not have a single recurrent sequence mutation; a low mutation burden does not mean benign behavior.

entities.name: Appendiceal neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Appendiceal NET has no reliable one-gene mnemonic.
entities.pitfall: No consistent defining recurrent driver established. Goblet cell adenocarcinoma is a different entity; low-grade NETs are included because they have malignant potential.

entities.name: Colorectal neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Rectal/colonic NET: low mutation burden and heterogeneous biology.
snv: Recurrent/candidate — PI3K–AKT pathway and chromatin-regulator alterations in small series; no universal driver
entities.pitfall: Do not substitute TP53/RB1-heavy NEC profiles for well-differentiated colorectal NETs.

entities.name: Digestive neuroendocrine carcinoma
entities.anchor: Poorly differentiated digestive NEC: TP53 and RB pathway disruption.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and RB1 inactivation (frequencies vary by site)
Driver — KRAS/BRAF activation and APC loss in subsets, particularly colorectal NEC
cnv: Cooperating — RB1 deletion; MYC or CCNE1 amplification (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Esophageal, gastric, intestinal, biliary and pancreatic small-/large-cell NEC are grouped; NET G3 is a different entity.

entities.name: Digestive mixed neuroendocrine–non-neuroendocrine neoplasm
entities.anchor: MiNEN components often share early carcinoma drivers.
snv: Driver/cooperating — site-dependent TP53, KRAS, APC, BRAF and/or RB1 alterations
entities.pitfall: MiNEN is a morphologic mixed-neoplasm category, not a single genetic disease. Not equivalent to appendiceal goblet cell adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Gastroblastoma
entities.anchor: Gastroblastoma: activate GLI via fusion.
rearr: Driver — MALAT1::GLI1 (characteristic); other GLI fusions reported
entities.pitfall: Rare low-grade malignant biphasic gastric tumor; a GLI1 fusion requires morphologic correlation.

entities.name: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type
entities.anchor: Common breast carcinoma: PIK3CA/TP53 and subtype-dependent amplifications.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA or AKT1 activating variants; PTEN loss (subsets)
Cooperating — TP53, GATA3 and MAP3K1 alterations
cnv: Driver — ERBB2/HER2 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — CCND1, FGFR1 or MYC amplification; RB1/PTEN deletion (subsets)
other: Predisposition — BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2 defects and homologous-recombination deficiency in subsets
entities.pitfall: ER/PR/HER2 and intrinsic expression classes are not separate histologic entities here; HER2 protein positivity and gene amplification are related but different tests.

entities.name: Invasive lobular carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Lobular: lose CDH1/E-cadherin.
snv: Driver — CDH1 inactivation
Cooperating — PIK3CA, PTEN, FOXA1 and TBX3 alterations
cnv: Characteristic — 16q/CDH1 loss; 1q gain
entities.pitfall: CDH1 loss is strongly characteristic but may arise through nonmutational mechanisms; pleomorphic and other variants are merged.

entities.name: Tubular carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Low-grade luminal pathway; no unique defining mutation.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA activating variants (subset)
cnv: Characteristic — 16q loss and 1q gain
entities.pitfall: Morphology defines tubular carcinoma; these alterations also occur in ordinary low-grade luminal breast cancer.

entities.name: Cribriform carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Low-grade luminal carcinoma with cribriform architecture.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA activating variants (subset)
cnv: Characteristic — low-grade luminal copy-number pattern; often 16q loss/1q gain
entities.pitfall: No distinct recurrent fusion established; do not confuse with adenoid cystic carcinoma.

entities.name: Mucinous carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Mucinous breast carcinoma: luminal biology without one defining gene.
snv: Recurrent — PIK3CA and GATA3 alterations in subsets
cnv: Characteristic — often relatively few copy-number changes
entities.pitfall: Pure and mixed forms differ; do not use mucinous histology to infer a specific mutation.

entities.name: Invasive micropapillary carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Micropapillary architecture is not a unique genomic driver.
snv: Driver/cooperating — PIK3CA and TP53 alterations (subsets)
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification in a subset
Characteristic — 1q gain and 16q loss may occur
entities.pitfall: Morphologic reverse polarity is different from the IDH2-defined tall-cell carcinoma with reversed polarity.

entities.name: Papillary carcinoma of breast, invasive
entities.anchor: Papillary invasive tumors often follow luminal PI3K signaling.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA or AKT1 activating variants (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Includes invasive papillary carcinoma and invasive components of solid/encapsulated papillary lesions; purely in situ lesions are outside this malignant-invasive scope.

entities.name: Carcinoma with apocrine differentiation of breast
entities.anchor: Apocrine: PI3K pathway and sometimes ERBB2.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA activation or PTEN loss (subsets)
Cooperating — TP53 alterations
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
other: Phenotype — androgen-receptor expression is common; expression is not a gene mutation
entities.pitfall: Apocrine morphology does not guarantee an ERBB2 amplification or a specific sequence driver.

entities.name: Metaplastic breast carcinoma
entities.anchor: Metaplastic breast: TP53 plus PI3K/Wnt-pathway disruption.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, PIK3CA, PIK3R1, PTEN, ARID1A and FAT1 alterations
cnv: Characteristic — complex gains/losses; EGFR amplification in a subset
entities.pitfall: Squamous, spindle, matrix-producing and other metaplastic patterns are merged; a triple-negative phenotype is not a mutation.

entities.name: Secretory carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Secretory breast: ETV6::NTRK3.
rearr: Driver — ETV6::NTRK3 (highly characteristic)
entities.pitfall: The same fusion occurs in other organ sites and infantile fibrosarcoma; morphology and site matter.

entities.name: Adenoid cystic carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Adenoid cystic breast: MYB activation.
rearr: Driver — MYB::NFIB; MYBL1 rearrangements in a subset
entities.pitfall: Often triple-negative but genomically different from ordinary high-grade triple-negative breast carcinoma.

entities.name: Acinic cell carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Breast acinic carcinoma resembles triple-negative breast cancer genomically.
snv: Cooperating — TP53 alterations; heterogeneous additional breast-cancer drivers
entities.pitfall: Do not assume salivary acinic NR4A3 rearrangement applies to the breast counterpart.

entities.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Breast mucoepidermoid is rare: fusion status varies between series.
snv: Driver — PIK3CA activating variants in a subset
rearr: Driver — CRTC1::MAML2 reported in a subset; other series lack MAML2 fusions
entities.pitfall: Evidence is limited and conflicting across small cohorts; do not memorize MAML2 as universal in breast MEC.

entities.name: Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity of breast
aliases: Solid papillary carcinoma with reverse polarity
entities.anchor: Reversed polarity: IDH2 R172, often with PIK3CA.
snv: Driver — IDH2 p.R172 hotspot
Cooperating — PIK3CA activation (frequent co-event)
entities.pitfall: Different from invasive micropapillary carcinoma and metastatic tall-cell papillary thyroid carcinoma.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine tumor of breast
entities.anchor: Breast NET often has luminal/chromatin alterations, not universal MEN1.
snv: Recurrent — FOXA1, TBX3, ARID1A and PIK3CA alterations (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Exclude metastasis from another organ. Older studies used broader definitions including carcinomas with neuroendocrine differentiation.

entities.name: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of breast
aliases: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of breast
entities.anchor: Breast NEC: TP53/RB pathway disruption.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 and RB1 inactivation, particularly in small-cell NEC
cnv: Cooperating — RB1 deletion; occasional MDM2/MDM4 amplification
entities.pitfall: Small-/large-cell NEC are merged; exclude metastatic pulmonary NEC and distinguish breast NET.

entities.name: Malignant adenomyoepithelioma of breast
entities.anchor: Biphasic breast tumor: HRAS Q61 plus PI3K-pathway changes.
snv: Driver — HRAS Q61 with PIK3CA/PIK3R1 alterations in ER-negative tumors
Driver — PIK3CA or AKT1 activation in some ER-positive tumors
entities.pitfall: These drivers also occur in benign adenomyoepithelioma and do not by themselves establish malignant transformation.

entities.name: Malignant phyllodes tumor
entities.anchor: Phyllodes: stromal MED12; progression often adds TERT.
snv: Driver — MED12 exon 2 variants (subset)
Progression — TERT promoter, TP53, RB1 or EGFR alterations
cnv: Progression — TERT or EGFR amplification (subset)
entities.pitfall: MED12 and TERT alterations occur in some nonmalignant fibroepithelial tumors; histology determines grade.

entities.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
aliases: Invasive encapsulated follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Papillary thyroid: BRAF/RAS or a kinase fusion.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E; NRAS/HRAS/KRAS variants (alternative subsets)
Progression — TERT promoter mutation (subset)
rearr: Driver — CCDC6::RET / NCOA4::RET; ETV6::NTRK3 and other NTRK fusions; BRAF fusions (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Histologic variants are merged. BRAF-like and RAS-like biology differ; a RAS mutation alone does not prove malignancy.

entities.name: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Follicular thyroid: RAS or PAX8::PPARG.
snv: Driver — NRAS/HRAS/KRAS activating variants
Cooperating/progression — PTEN, EIF1AX or TERT promoter variants (subsets)
rearr: Driver — PAX8::PPARG (subset)
entities.pitfall: RAS and PAX8::PPARG can occur in nonmalignant follicular tumors; invasion establishes carcinoma.

entities.name: Oncocytic thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Oncocytic/Hürthle: mitochondrial complex I plus chromosome loss.
snv: Driver/characteristic — mitochondrial complex-I gene variants (MT-ND genes)
Cooperating — TERT promoter, TP53, NRAS and DAXX alterations (subsets)
cnv: Characteristic — widespread chromosome losses / near-haploidy, sometimes followed by genome doubling
entities.pitfall: A distinct entity from ordinary follicular carcinoma; mitochondrial variants require appropriate testing and interpretation.

entities.name: Differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Differentiated lineage plus progression events such as TERT.
snv: Driver — BRAF or RAS pathway alterations retained from differentiated precursor
Progression — TERT promoter and TP53 alterations (subsets)
rearr: Driver — retained RET/NTRK or other kinase fusions in a subset
entities.pitfall: High grade is defined by mitotic activity/necrosis while retaining differentiation; not synonymous with anaplastic carcinoma.

entities.name: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: RAS/BRAF background plus TERT and additional tumor-suppressor hits.
snv: Driver — NRAS/HRAS/KRAS or BRAF activation
Progression/cooperating — TERT promoter, TP53, EIF1AX, PI3K-pathway alterations
rearr: Driver — RET, NTRK or other kinase fusions (minor subset)
entities.pitfall: Diagnosis is morphologic; no single mutation distinguishes it from differentiated or anaplastic carcinoma.

entities.name: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Anaplastic thyroid: TP53/TERT with accumulated MAPK and PI3K alterations.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E or RAS activation (subsets)
Progression/cooperating — TP53, TERT promoter, PIK3CA/PTEN and SWI/SNF/chromatin-gene alterations
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B loss and heterogeneous focal amplifications
entities.pitfall: Includes primary thyroid squamous carcinoma in WHO 5th; not every tumor is BRAF-mutant.

entities.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Medullary: RET point mutation, not the usual papillary RET fusion.
snv: Driver — RET activating variants (somatic or germline; M918T and cysteine variants are examples)
Driver — HRAS/KRAS activation in some RET-wild-type tumors
entities.pitfall: Germline RET causes MEN2; a tumor RET result alone does not determine whether a variant is inherited.

entities.name: Cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma
aliases: Cribriform morular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Cribriform–morular: APC/CTNNB1 and nuclear beta-catenin.
snv: Driver — APC inactivation (germline or somatic); CTNNB1 activation in a subset
entities.pitfall: WHO 5th treats it as distinct from papillary thyroid carcinoma; association with FAP is not universal.

entities.name: Thyroblastoma
entities.anchor: Thyroid embryonal tumor: DICER1.
snv: Driver — DICER1 RNase IIIb hotspot plus a second inactivating event (characteristic pattern)
entities.pitfall: Formerly malignant teratoid tumor of thyroid; evidence base is small and morphology is essential.

entities.name: Spindle epithelial tumor with thymus-like differentiation
entities.anchor: SETTLE: no established recurrent genomic hallmark.
entities.pitfall: SS18::SSX supports synovial sarcoma, not SETTLE. Metastases can occur late despite bland histology.

entities.name: Intrathyroidal thymic carcinoma
entities.anchor: Thymic differentiation in the thyroid has no defining recurrent driver.
entities.pitfall: CD5/CD117 immunophenotype is not proof of KIT mutation; molecular evidence is limited.

entities.name: Secretory carcinoma of thyroid
entities.anchor: Thyroid secretory carcinoma: ETV6::NTRK3.
rearr: Driver — ETV6::NTRK3
entities.pitfall: NTRK-rearranged papillary thyroid carcinoma is a different histologic diagnosis despite a shared fusion.

entities.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of thyroid
entities.anchor: Thyroid mucoepidermoid carcinoma has no consistent site-wide driver.
entities.pitfall: Rare and heterogeneous; do not automatically assign the salivary MAML2 hallmark or merge with sclerosing MEC with eosinophilia.

entities.name: Sclerosing mucoepidermoid carcinoma with eosinophilia
entities.anchor: SMECE: a distinct rare thyroid tumor without a reliable mutation mnemonic.
entities.pitfall: Common thyroid drivers and MAML2 rearrangements were absent in a dedicated series; isolated mutation reports do not establish a universal driver.

entities.name: Parathyroid carcinoma
entities.anchor: Parathyroid carcinoma: CDC73/parafibromin.
snv: Driver — CDC73 biallelic inactivation (somatic or germline-plus-somatic)
cnv: Driver — CDC73 deletion or allelic loss (can also be copy-neutral LOH)
entities.pitfall: CDC73 loss supports a high-risk pathway but can occur in adenomas; malignancy requires invasion/metastatic criteria.

entities.name: Adrenocortical carcinoma
entities.anchor: Adrenal cortex: TP53, Wnt and IGF2 dysregulation.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53, CTNNB1, PRKAR1A, MEN1 and RB1 alterations (subsets)
cnv: Driver/cooperating — ZNRF3 deletion; CDKN2A/RB1 losses; TERT, CDK4 or CCNE1 amplification (subsets)
other: Epigenetic — IGF2 overexpression often relates to 11p15 imprinting/allelic changes
entities.pitfall: Common benign adrenal adenoma drivers should not be assumed to define carcinoma; variants are merged.

entities.name: Pheochromocytoma
entities.anchor: Adrenal medulla: pseudohypoxia, kinase or Wnt routes.
snv: Driver — RET, NF1, HRAS, VHL, SDHx, MAX, TMEM127, FH or EPAS1 alterations (alternative subsets)
Cooperating — ATRX alterations in a subset
cnv: Driver — second-allele losses/deletions involving susceptibility genes (subset)
rearr: Driver — UBTF::MAML3 and other MAML3 fusions (rare subset)
entities.pitfall: All have metastatic potential; histology and driver mutation alone cannot label a tumor metastatic. Germline and somatic mechanisms must be distinguished.

entities.name: Paraganglioma
entities.anchor: Extra-adrenal paraganglioma: remember SDHx, especially SDHB risk.
snv: Driver — SDHB, SDHD, SDHC, SDHA, SDHAF2, VHL, FH or EPAS1 alterations (subsets)
Cooperating — ATRX/TERT alterations can accompany aggressive behavior
cnv: Driver — second-allele loss/deletion involving SDHx or other susceptibility genes
entities.pitfall: Sympathetic and parasympathetic tumors are merged; all have metastatic potential. SDHB loss is a pathway marker, not proof of a germline SDHB variant.

entities.name: Metastatic pituitary neuroendocrine tumor
entities.anchor: Metastatic PitNET: TP53/ATRX and lineage-dependent alterations.
snv: Cooperating/progression — ATRX and TP53 inactivation in subsets
cnv: Cooperating — ATRX deletions and heterogeneous copy-number changes
entities.pitfall: Formerly pituitary carcinoma. Metastasis, not local invasion or one mutation, establishes this category; ordinary nonmetastatic PitNETs are excluded.

entities.name: Pituitary blastoma
entities.anchor: Infantile pituitary blastoma: DICER1 two-hit pattern.
snv: Driver — germline DICER1 loss-of-function plus somatic RNase IIIb hotspot (typical pattern)
entities.pitfall: An embryonal tumor distinct from PitNET; rare adult cases exist and not every case has a demonstrable germline variant.

coverage.basis: WHO fifth-edition broad entities, with histologic variants collapsed and molecular literature checked on 2026-10-19. WHO online lists a sixth-edition Digestive volume; this file is not a sixth-edition reconciliation.
merged: Lung adenocarcinoma histologic variants collapsed; sarcomatoid patterns grouped, with pulmonary blastoma retained for distinct molecular teaching.
Thymoma A/AB/B1–B3 combined; thymic carcinoma subtypes combined.
GI adenocarcinoma histologic patterns grouped by site; digestive NEC and MiNEN represented as site-family records with searchable site aliases.
Breast papillary invasive patterns grouped; separate in situ lesions excluded.
Thyroid variants and PitNET hormonal lineages collapsed; primary thyroid squamous carcinoma included with anaplastic carcinoma.
excluded: In situ neoplasia, dysplasia, benign tumors and uncertain/intermediate-behavior lesions, including NIFTP, thyroid tumors of uncertain malignant potential, benign/borderline phyllodes tumors and nonmetastatic ordinary PitNET.
Organ-site lymphomas, germ-cell tumors, melanomas and mesenchymal tumors are cross-system entities intended to be represented in the companion hematology, germ-cell and soft-tissue/bone sections.
Metastases to these organs are not duplicated as new entities.
limitations: Broad-entity study abstraction is not a line-by-line reproduction or guarantee of every WHO subtype or newly provisional entity.

Rare pulmonary epithelial-myoepithelial, thyroid thymic-like/mucoepidermoid and some NET entities have limited molecular data; empty arrays explicitly indicate no established characteristic recurrent alteration for memorization.
Alteration lists are representative established drivers/cooperating events, not a full mutation catalog; no frequencies or treatment recommendations are supplied.

Thymomas, carcinoids/NETs, paragangliomas and solid pseudopapillary neoplasms are included despite variable or indolent behavior because of their malignant classification/potential; metastatic status cannot be inferred from a listed mutation.
Some minor/common histologic breast-type profiles and rare digestive epithelial entities rely on broader study cohorts rather than entity-exclusive large series.
